study type: Retrospective cohort study (secondary analysis of a multicentre CD registry)
exposure: CD after labour vs. no labour
CD performed between 7 pm and 7 am
increasing American Society of Anesthesiologists category
cohort: The study included 57,182 women who underwent Caesarean delivery from a multicentre registry.
finding: The study identified several modifiable and non-modifiable risk factors associated with Caesarean delivery surgical site infection, with an overall SSI rate of 6.5%.
mod_finding: Primary CD and CD after labour were associated with higher SSI rates, while low transverse CD was associated with a decreased rate of SSI.
